soundness_flags.label: def:regularized-hessian-estimator; thm:uniform-margin-band
soundness_flags.one_line: A signed high-order smoothing operator need not preserve positive definiteness, so \widehat H_p^{-1} and hence \widehat\gamma_{pq} are undefined on samples outside \mathcal B_n despite the claimed everywhere-defined estimator.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: oeq:global-endpoint-response; thm:uniform-margin-band; thm:sharp-separation-lower
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The boundary-uniform endpoint Hessian response and quadratic remainder remain open, and only the upper band and upper separation inequality rely on them.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The lower separation bound is unconditional; the simultaneous upper band and matching upper separation rate are claimed only conditional on an affirmative endpoint-response result.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the signed-smoothed Hessian by an explicitly positive-definite reported field, for example spectral clipping at m/4, and prove that clipping is inactive on the band event before defining every inverse and certificate.
Make the admissible f,g class and the two-resolution bias-variance calculation explicit, including why k_n yields the claimed Hessian radius after the logarithmic endpoint-response loss.
Retrieve and cite the exact NeurIPS proceedings version of the dynamic-OT paper, then align its theorem numbering and displayed assumptions with the cited counterexample target.

recommended_next_step: Revise the estimator so its inverse is defined on every sample, make the rate calculation auditable, and then continue this field-tier angle.
